title: AGENT-CORPUS-ADMISSION: which agent corpus may enter the pipeline, under what rule set, and does the BFCL-Result 2025-12-16 multi_turn archive pass the zero-call pilot? (plan A10; the rule set (a)-(e) and its first application)
question: Before any agent corpus is judged, the record needs (1) a rule set under which a corpus is ADMITTED, refused or admitted for description only, verified by command on ingested tables ((a) split, (b) checker output table, (c) termination as a class, (d) the judged artefact under a declared cap, (e) designed stratum), and (2) a first application: a zero-call pilot on the BFCL-Result 2025-12-16 multi_turn archive deciding which strata may carry JUDGED cells and which are PREDICTIVE-ONLY. The pilot judges nothing and ranks nothing.

plain_description.what: Writes a five-point rule set that an agent benchmark (tool-using AI agents) must pass before it may be judged, and applies it without any judge calls to one archive: 8 agents x 800 multi-turn tasks from the BFCL function-calling leaderboard (Dec 2025), using a 300-episode sample.
plain_description.why: Extending the thesis from question answering to agents needs a gate so that unusable or badly specified agent data does not enter the evaluation pipeline.
plain_description.information: A pass would let agent data enter the pipeline; a failure names exactly what is missing. Result: done; NOT admitted as-is. Four of five rules were verified, but the per-episode size cap for what the judge would read was never declared (the author's decision), and all four task groups are description-only for now (the 'base' group passed only at its point estimate); nothing was ranked or judged.
